opening.name: Opening & Rapport
opening.goal: Establish authority, transfer belief, and set proper frame while building trust

bridges.text: I promise that I will do my absolute best to give you a high return on your attention because it's the most valuable thing you have
My goal here isn't for you to buy, but for you to decide - for you, not for me. I'll be the same either way
I want to help you help yourself. There's a difference - it's nuanced but it's real
I use a lot of rapport and humor in my selling, and I'd be like 'hey [name]...' [insert situational humor]

recovery: What brings you here today - are you just hopping on calls for information, or is there a problem you're trying to solve?
Do you do this all the time - hop on lots of different programs to find out information - or is there something specific you're looking for?

discovery.name: Discovery & Pain Points
discovery.goal: Identify core pain, amplify consequences, and establish what they really want

bridges.text: What are you most afraid of having happen if you don't solve this?
How long have you been struggling with this? How's another [timeframe] sound if nothing changes?
Are you tired of another year of 'almost'? Almost hitting your goals, almost getting to [specific outcome]?
Do you think you're in this position because you've struggled to make decisions in the past?
What would need to happen in the first 90 days for you to feel confident this was the right decision?

recovery: Help me understand - what's the real problem you're trying to solve here?
Let's get specific - what does success look like for you?
What happens if you don't fix this in the next year?

presentation.name: Solution Presentation
presentation.goal: Present solution with logical proof and value demonstration

bridges.text: How many people would you need to see for it to be more unreasonable not to believe than to believe? 10? 50? Here's a thousand - tell me when to stop
This isn't about whether this works - I've already proven that. The question is whether you work
You're going to learn these lessons either way - do you want it to take 12 weeks or 12 years?
Edison took however long to make a light bulb, then we just bought the lesson from him. That's how civilization moves faster
There's no entrepreneur school, no one teaches this stuff, but there are people who teach it for this specific industry

recovery: What questions do you have about how this actually works?
What would you need to see to believe this is possible for you?
Does this make logical sense so far?

objection.name: Objection Handling
objection.goal: Address logical concerns using Hormozi's 5 distortion framework

bridges.text: The reason you're telling yourself not to do this is the reason you should do it
Don't let a bad decision burn you twice - once when you made the poor investment, but a second time when you let that stop you from a good investment
You're asking for permission instead of support. It's your life, not theirs
If you didn't get a gasp from the price, you didn't go high enough
The fact that it's a lot for you is good - it means you're going to try hard
Every self-made billionaire started with nothing, just like you. The difference wasn't resources, it was being resourceful
When then is a logical fallacy - like saying 'I'll save money when I'm rich'

recovery: Help me understand what you're really afraid of
Is there something I haven't explained clearly enough?

closing.name: Closing & Next Steps
closing.goal: Help them make a decision and take ownership of their choice

bridges.text: Let's make the decision together. Do you believe this will help you achieve what you want? Do you trust me to fulfill my word? Do you think it'll work for you?
You're only one decision away from changing your life forever
Which risk-free option do you want - the one that guarantees you won't get there, or the one that has potential to get you where you want to go?
Do you think making this decision will get you closer or further from your goal?
If I was giving you a Ferrari for $5,000 right now, you'd find the money. So find the money - let's do it
Either you win or you learn, and both get you closer to where you want to go

recovery: What's holding you back from saying yes right now?
What would need to change for this to be a definite yes?
Are we going to do this together or not?

logical_buyer.approach: Use statistical proof, logical frameworks, and step-by-step reasoning
logical_buyer.closing_style: Three-question close: believe it works, trust me, works for you

emotional_buyer.approach: Transfer belief and conviction, use stories and social proof

skeptical_buyer.approach: Address distortions systematically, use 'don't let it burn you twice'

conviction_framework.principle: Selling is a transference of belief over a bridge of trust
requirements: You must believe to transfer belief
Conviction must be deeper than their excuses
conviction_framework.application: Fill your own conviction first, then transfer through certainty and care

power_distortion_framework.principle: People cast power to three sources: circumstances, others, self
power_distortion_framework.approach: Peel layers from surface to core, address each systematically

value_equation.formula: Dream Outcome + Perceived Likelihood - Time Delay - Effort & Sacrifice = Value
value_equation.application: Maximize dream outcome and likelihood while minimizing time and effort
value_equation.positioning: Position solution as highest value using this equation

decision_framework.principle: Deciding means 'to cut off' - which future are we killing?
three_questions: Do you believe this will help you achieve what you want?
Do you trust me to fulfill my word?
Do you think it will work for you?
decision_framework.close: If yes to all three, moral obligation to help them get the money

stall_recovery: I need to think about it → This isn't a fast decision - you've been making this decision for [timeframe]. How long do you want [problem] to be on your list?
Not a good time → Totally understand. Do you think you're going to be busy again in the future? Then don't you think it's best to start now when you are busy?
Can't afford it → The fact that it's a lot for you is good. Every self-made person started with nothing - it's about being resourceful, not having resources
Need to talk to spouse → Are you asking for permission or support? They're not happy with your current struggle, why would they oppose something that fixes it?

mirroring.technique: Step into their shoes first, then walk them through your epiphany
mirroring.example: I used to feel the same way... I found this out... it's a logical fallacy called...
mirroring.purpose: Not attacking them, helping them from the inside out

labeling.childlike_curiosity: When someone objects: 'Huh, that's so weird, I wouldn't have thought that. Tell me more about that'
labeling.seek_understanding: Seek to understand, not to argue. Maintain curiosity even in high-stakes moments
labeling.emotional_labeling: What are you most afraid of having happen? What's the worst thing you envision?

calibrated_questions: What are you most afraid of having happen if you buy?
What would need to happen in the first 90 days for you to feel confident?
How many people would you need to see for it to be more unreasonable not to believe?
Do you think making this decision gets you closer or further from your goal?
What's different between perfect and what we've got here?
If the rules were reversed and your [spouse] needed this, would you support them?

stories.narrative: Sarah was a CFO at a manufacturing company, incredibly skeptical about ROI claims. She said 'I've heard these promises before.' So I asked her, 'What would need to happen in the first 90 days for you to feel confident this was the right decision?' That simple question changed everything. She gave me exact success metrics, we built our proposal around those. Six months later, she became our biggest advocate.
stories.lesson: Ask prospects to define their own success criteria

stories.narrative: In Shoe Dog, Phil Knight was about to lose Nike multiple times. This one time he needed tremendous money, maxed all credit, banks wouldn't lend. Instead of giving up, he went to his vendors and said 'You need to pay my payroll for me because otherwise I'll be out of business.' He was resourceful, not resource-dependent.
stories.lesson: Every self-made billionaire started with nothing - success is about resourcefulness
stories.impact: Eliminates money objections by shifting mindset

stories.narrative: I was with Layla at Sephora, saw two 12-15 year old girls getting excited about makeup. Staff member said 'Now that you're becoming women, you need to start budgeting for this stuff every month.' Girls were thrilled - 'We're becoming women!' When you have new identity, you have new priorities.
stories.lesson: Identity change requires priority change - alignment with who you want to become
stories.impact: Helps prospects step into new identity with new spending patterns

stories.narrative: Girl texted yesterday: 'Crazy to think I had a sales call with you six years ago and I'm kicking myself for not jumping on this.' I said 'You let a bad decision burn you twice - once when you made the poor investment, second when you let that stop you from a good investment.'
stories.lesson: Don't let past failures prevent future success
stories.impact: Overcomes objections based on previous bad experiences

statistics.data: Top 5 red zone offenses made playoffs 90% of the time over last 5 years
statistics.context: Closing ability makes up for deficiencies in other business areas
statistics.application: Emphasize importance of closing skills development

statistics.data: 10% never buy, 10% always buy, fight for middle 80%
statistics.context: Focus training and energy on the persuadable majority
statistics.application: Set realistic expectations and focus efforts appropriately

statistics.data: 100% of successful people started with same resources as you: nothing
statistics.context: Resources don't predict success, resourcefulness does

metaphors.metaphor: Peeling an onion - surface excuses (circumstances) → others → self → core truth
metaphors.explanation: Objections start with external blame, move to others, finally to self - peel each layer
metaphors.usage: Navigate from surface objections to core decision-making

metaphors.metaphor: Edison's light bulb lesson - he took time to learn, we buy the lesson to save time
metaphors.explanation: Human civilization advances by buying others' lessons rather than learning from scratch

metaphors.metaphor: 'Decide' means 'to cut off' - which future are we killing today?
metaphors.explanation: Every decision kills alternative futures - choose which one to eliminate
metaphors.usage: Frame decision-making as active choice, not passive waiting

metaphors.metaphor: Each skill/program is a brick in the bridge from where you are to where you want to be
metaphors.explanation: No single program is salvation, but each gets you closer to your goal
metaphors.usage: Set realistic expectations while maintaining momentum

humor.technique: Self-deprecating about success story: 'My life has gone significantly better - I went from sleeping on gym floor to my mom's basement (actually penthouse)'
humor.effect: Breaks tension and creates relatability despite success

humor.technique: Exaggerated nightmare scenario: 'If your husband says he wants you to stay overweight, sit on couch with Cheetos fingers, create generational unhealth...'
humor.effect: Makes ridiculous objection obvious through absurd extension

humor.technique: Worst case scenario joke: 'I take your credit card, swipe as much as possible, go to Vegas, put it all on black, then Monaco where they can't extradite me'
humor.effect: Breaks tension around fear while identifying real concern

psychology.mechanism: Selling is transference of belief over bridge of trust
psychology.application: Must believe deeply yourself before you can transfer belief to others
psychology.ethics: Only transfer belief in something that truly helps them

psychology.mechanism: People cast power to external sources when they feel powerless
psychology.application: Help them reclaim power by addressing each distortion systematically
psychology.ethics: Return power to them for their benefit, not your sale

psychology.mechanism: Albert Ellis's 3 core distortions: circumstances must be perfect, others must treat me fairly, I must do well or I'm no good
psychology.application: Identify which distortion they're operating from and address the logic
psychology.ethics: Help them see reality clearly, not manipulate their thinking

psychology.mechanism: People's spending reflects their identity and predicts their future
psychology.application: Help them align spending with desired identity, not current one
psychology.ethics: Guide toward beneficial identity shifts, not wasteful spending

recovery.response: Totally understand. What are the main criteria you're thinking through? Let's think about it right now - I'm here, I'm the only source of information you have
recovery.technique: Remove time delay by providing immediate information access

recovery.response: If this were perfect, would you do it? [Get yes] Then what's different between perfect and what we've got here?
recovery.followup: Address specific gaps or realize it's not about the program

recovery.response: The fact that it's a lot for you is good - it means you're going to try hard. If it does what we say, is it worth it? [Yes] Great, then it's not about price, it's about whether you believe me
recovery.technique: Reframe price as commitment indicator, then isolate real objection
recovery.followup: Provide more proof or address trust issues

recovery.response: What do you think they wouldn't like about this? [Listen] Are they happy with your current struggle? Why would they oppose something that fixes what already makes them unhappy?
recovery.technique: Isolate objection and reframe as support vs permission
recovery.followup: Position as better partner through self-improvement

recovery.response: Totally understand. Do you want this to last long-term? Do you think you'll be busy again in the future? Then don't you think it's best to start when you're busy?
recovery.followup: Emphasize need for support during busy periods

word_choice.etymology: Latin 'decidere' - to cut off, to kill off
word_choice.power: Frames decision as actively choosing which future to eliminate
word_choice.usage: Which future are we killing off today - your dreams or your current struggle?

word_choice.psychology: Implies return and growth vs cost and expense
word_choice.power: Reframes spending as value-building rather than money loss
word_choice.usage: This investment in yourself compounds over time and can never be taken from you

word_choice.power: Shifts from victim mindset to empowerment mindset
word_choice.usage: Every successful person started with nothing - it's about being resourceful, not having resources

word_choice.psychology: Progress vs perfection, direction vs destination
word_choice.power: Reduces perfectionism and fear of wrong choice
word_choice.usage: Do you think this gets you closer or further from your goal? We don't need to be snipers, just directionally right

time_objections.core: When/then logical fallacy - waiting for perfect circumstances
approach: Macro: Always busy, need support when busy
Micro: Phone shows actual time usage
When/then: Logical fallacy like 'save money when rich'
time_objections.close: You're going to be busy forever - wouldn't you want the most help when you need it most?

approach: Lot is good: means you'll try
You'll buy the program anyway - 12 weeks or 12 years
money_objections.close: Every self-made person started with nothing - find the money like you do for emergencies

approach: Change the change - what you've been doing created current results
Hypothetical: if perfect would you do it
fit_objections.close: Are you in enough pain? Is staying the same worse than changing?

authority_objections.core: Asking permission instead of requesting support
approach: Are they happy with current struggle
authority_objections.close: If you don't own this decision, you'll blame them when nothing changes

avoidance_objections.core: Fear of making wrong decision or inability to decide
approach: Past: not fast decision, sunk cost
Future: which option gets you closer
avoidance_objections.close: Which risk-free option - guaranteed failure or potential success?
